prompt: A regular pentagon tabletop has sides of $8$ inches and an apothem (the distance from the center to the middle of a side) of $5.5$ inches. What is its area, in square inches?
hint: A regular polygon's area can be found from its perimeter and its apothem. Recall the formula that joins them.

hints.text: A regular polygon's area can be found from its perimeter and its apothem. Recall the formula that joins them.
The formula is $A = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{perimeter} \times \text{apothem}$. The perimeter is $5 \times 8 = 40$ inches, so work out $\frac{1}{2}(40)(5.5)$.
$\frac{1}{2}(40)(5.5) = 20 \times 5.5 = 110$, so the tabletop has an area of $110$ square inches.

explanation: A regular pentagon has five equal sides, so its perimeter is $P = 5 \times 8 = 40$ inches.
The area of a regular polygon is $A = \frac{1}{2}Pa$, which here is $\frac{1}{2}(40)(5.5)$.
Half of $40$ is $20$, and $20 \times 5.5 = 110$, so the area is $110$ square inches.

alternativeExplanations.title: Five triangles from the center
steps: Draw segments from the center to each corner: the pentagon becomes $5$ identical triangles, each with base $8$ and height $5.5$ (the apothem).
One triangle is $\frac{1}{2}(8)(5.5) = 22$ sq in, and $5 \times 22 = 110$ sq in. That is exactly what the $\frac{1}{2}Pa$ formula packages up.
